summary: Marquette County, MI tower erected near Ives Lake by October 1922; a 1955 survey station description calls it abandoned. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Described as an abandoned lookout tower in a 1955 federal survey station description.

events.note: Erected by October 1922, per a L'Anse Sentinel item quoted by Forest Lookouts; the state was installing a telephone line to it
1955 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description calls it an abandoned lookout tower; the date it was abandoned is not given

evidence.supports: erected by October 1922; state installing telephone line
evidence.quote: A fire tower has been erected near Ives Lake, Marquette county and a telephone is being installed by the state to connect with Big Bay.

evidence.supports: watchman planned for fire season; view covers a large area
evidence.quote: At this observation tower a watchman will be stationed during the season of fires, his observation covering a vast acreage.
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1955 (NET)
THE LOCATION OF AN ABANDONED LOOKOUT TOWER AND U.S. LAKE SURVEY TRIANGULATION STATION IVES HILL 1872.

evidence.supports: survey mark about a mile southeast of Ives Lake on a wooded hill
evidence.quote: MILE SOUTHEAST OF IVES LAKE ON THE HIGHEST POINT OF A WOODED HILL AT

evidence.supports: survey measured from the tower's anchor legs
evidence.quote: SOUTHEAST OF THE SOUTHWEST ANCHOR LEG OF THE ABANDONED LOOKOUT TOWER AND 11.5 FEET SOUTHWEST OF THE SOUTHEAST ANCHOR LEG.

notes_for_editor: The record's point (46.8238, -87.8348) may sit at the lake. The 1955 station description places the tower on a wooded hill about a mile southeast of Ives Lake, so the point should be checked against that. No source names the agency; the 1922 item says only 'the state', so agency is left out. Status 'abandoned' comes from a 1955 description and is the latest word found; condition today is unknown. All material comes from one page quoting a 1922 newspaper and a 1955 NGS description.
